_about: Every parameter of the router table (#6740), read by build.py. Data, not code: change a number here and re-run. A route's outcome is acceptance judged against the page image (route-judge pilot, #7376), not agreement with Opus. Opus is the judge, not the reference reader. The hierarchical models (v1, v2) give only the weak prior.

prior._about: Acceptance prior per route. Draft served as-is: v1's P(passes the absolute floors) for the draft engine in its chart. Draft plus corrector: d + (1 - d) x v2's median net gain for that corrector in that cell (d = the draft's prior mean, 0.5 if v1 has no chart). Worth pages_measured pages (a + b) when every input is measured, pages_pooled when any is pooled. Flat Beta(1, 1) where neither model covers the route (translation, Tibetan drafts).
prior._v1_charts_left_out: German and French OCR have no v1 chart: latin-script-other is web-transcribed text and gives Flash-Lite 0.998, against 17/30 the judge accepted on Latin. Chinese print: v1 says its floors measure the reference panel's variant forms.

_cluster_note: The judge's pages are not independent within a book. When a route's n pages come from fewer books (Latin: 30 pages in 9 books), k and n are scaled by books / n before they enter the posterior. Wrong-text pages are read as the page count k of n.

evidence_rules._about: Which earlier tests enter, and how (#7263 backfill-all, 2026-10-28; the 214 judged write-ups are classified on #7263). (1) Instrument: per-page verdicts against the page IMAGE, by an Opus judge, that split accept from wrong text (route-judge accept / wrong_text; Step T or Step C misleading; judge.py MISLEADING; MQM material; a serious-error flag). A 1-5 or 0-5 score, a CER or accuracy against a typed reference, and a better / same / worse judgment do not enter: the first two feed the v1 / v2 priors where they feed anything. A Gemini-only judge does not enter (#6561: 5 of 5 of its 'invented' calls checked by eye were printed text). (2) The frame: pages drawn as the lane draws them; a set selected FOR difficulty (disagreement, changed pages, a CER bin, a detector flag) does not enter. (3) Stored per-page verdicts in the repo; counts quoted only in a write-up do not enter. (4) A test of another prompt or model than the route's enters as ITS OWN route (Arabic: the #6544 diplomatic READ prompt is agy-flash-low-read-diplomatic, not agy-flash-low-read). (5) The same route measured under another prompt or model vintage than the one that made, or will make, the cell's pages enters at `weight` (below) of its books: a fresh Flash-Lite read standing in for the stored lite drafts (#6553, #7341). (6) Sources drawn from the same books form one `book_group`, scaled together by the group's books / its pages, so no book counts twice (the pilot's 30 Latin pages are 30 of #5924's 250). (7) Every judged reading of a route counts once; a reading a packet copied from an earlier step does not count again (#5924 Step C2 / C4).

switch._about: Reference = the measured route with the highest posterior mean acceptance. Pick the cheapest measured route with P(acc_route >= acc_reference - within) >= p AND wrong-text pages / n <= wrong_text_max. The pick is the current route: keep. Another route: switch. None qualifies: keep.
switch._within: 2026-10-28 (Derek: 'prioritize cost a bit more'): 0.05 -> 0.08, and wrong_text_max 0.02 -> 0.04. At 0.05/0.02 German Flash-Lite correction stayed on Opus although agy Flash-low tied it (28/30 each; wrong text 2/30 vs 1/30, one page). The new margins move that cell only; Latin lite (30/30 vs 24/30), German 3 Flash (29/29 vs 26/30), Chinese Paddle and Tibetan translation keep Opus because their gaps exceed them.
switch._wrong_text_bar: relative (Derek, 2026-10-26: cost is part of the measure): a route passes when its wrong-text rate is at most the best route's rate + wrong_text_max, so the cheaper of two equally good routes wins. absolute: at most wrong_text_max outright, which keeps the current route whenever every route misses 2% (Tibetan: 3/30 on both correctors). The other bar is reported as a sensitivity.
switch._pick: 2026-10-26b (Derek: 'and this takes cost into account?' -> 'yes'): among the routes that pass the gate, the pick is the lowest median expected dollars per ACCEPTED page, one unit for every channel (was: the lowest share of the channel's free week per RAW page). The margin is unchanged; sensitivity_within reports what a 0.10 margin would pick, flagged when that route is 0.05-0.10 below the best and >= sensitivity_cheaper times cheaper.

hold._about: HOLD when no measured route has P(acceptance >= hold.acc) >= hold.p.

test_next._about: score(cell) = max over routes that draw capacity of pages_waiting x share_per_page x Var(acceptance posterior); share_per_page = the route's draw per page / its channel's free week. A test is pages_per_test pages of each named route, plus one Opus judge call per output.
test_next.routes: the cell's untested routes; if every route is tested, the one with the largest share x variance

fees._about: Turns points and agy calls into dollars for the pick only. --fees <private fee file> (agy_month_usd, claude_usd_per_weekly_point; the file route_ocr_v1.py reads) when present; else every plan at default_plan_month_usd, the list price v2 and #7417 assumed. The source used is named in the table; dollar results go to stdout only, never into the repo.

size_model._about: Inbox 2026-10-26 17:21Z and 17:22Z (Derek: '10 pages are not the same in all books'; 'maybe 5 when it is multi column'). A Claude call costs k x (overhead + the tokens of each page in it), tokens weighted input + output_weight x output. Batching saves the overhead only: points per page = k x (overhead / pages per call + the page's own tokens). Page sizes per cell: page-size.mjs (draft characters, image pixels -> image tokens by Anthropic's resize rule, OCR <columns> tag). k is fitted from the meter readings below. The Claude weekly quota is NOT published per token: k is an estimate, and the spread of the readings is its range.
size_model._central: Central k per kind of call = the median of that kind's readings. The two image readings agree (pilot, correct.mjs); the translation lane's own reading implies a rate about 3x lower: less per-call overhead (no images to open) or the coarse integer meter. Pricing translation at the image rate would contradict its one direct measurement, so each kind keeps its own; the range spans all readings.
size_model._output_weight: Opus list price: output tokens cost 5x input. Assumes the weekly meter weighs them as the API price does (unpublished).

overhead.basis: the pilot's one-page Opus image call, 14.6K in / 1.5K out tokens (route-judge pilot meter), minus one page: image about 1.5K + draft about 0.7K tokens in, about 0.75K out. The rest is the claude -p system prompt, the instructions and the tool turns that open the files, paid once per call.

chars_per_token_default._basis: used where fewer than min_pages_for_measured_cpt pages record Gemini's output token count. Chinese and Tibetan: one token a character, a guess (Gemini's measured 1.56 on Chinese 3 Flash includes the tag markup). Claude's tokenizer differs from Gemini's; neither is measured here for Claude.

pages_per_call._basis: Derek 2026-10-26: 10 for single-column prose, 5 for multi-column pages (two-column print, tables, glossed or interlinear). A cell's effective figure mixes the two by its measured multi-column share (OCR <columns>N</columns> with N >= 2, self-reported, or page_type table). correct.mjs (--per-call, default 10) and claude-translate.mjs (--per-call=10) have no layout switch today: 5 for multi-column is the rule proposed here, not what the lanes do.

readings.basis: route-judge pilot meter: weekly 21% -> 25% over 323 calls on a shared account, an UPPER bound
capacity.json opus-5.5@10: about 1% of an account-week per 250 Latin pages (#7258, integer meter)
capacity.json opus-translate@10: 3% of an account-week per 3,250 pages (#7263); another early reading is about 10x this

readings.why: Sonnet, not Opus, and no token counts recorded for those calls: it cannot fit an Opus rate

idle._about: Per channel, the share of THIS week's quota projected to go unused at the reset (allocate_v2.idle_shares: used / elapsed share of the week, per account). Idle pages cost 0 in the this-week decision. --idle claude=<share>,agy=<share> overrides.

claude._note: the first that reads in the {as_of, accounts[{account, weekly_percent, resets_at}]} shape; ops_reports claude-limits:latest on Mongo is the same reading (needs credentials, not read by this stdlib script).

agy.why: agy meter not read: it is on Hetzner main (/root/agy-quota), not on the job box; 0 = no idle credit

taxonomy: O1 confabulation (text not on the page); O4 block repetition; O5 silent omission; O6 meaning-changing misread; O7 numerals/dates wrong; O8 normalisation toward the expected; O10 secondary script dropped; O11 page furniture mis-tagged; O12 marginalia/apparatus dropped or mis-tagged; O16 self-reported tags wrong; I5 several leaves in one photo; T6 catchword/split-word seams; T8 sense inverted or qualifier dropped; T9 quiet omission; T10 invented scholarship in notes; T15 continuity meta wrong; E2 other. Full list: .claude/docs/page-error-taxonomy.md and judge.mjs TAXONOMY.
